hypothesis: Consecutive-loss streak + tight-spread conditioned skip: skip the open leg of an oracle signal when EITHER (a) the last 2 consecutive closed positions both had negative estimated PnL (streak signal), OR (b) current spread > 1.1x rolling 60-tick median (spread signal). Reduce-only orders always execute. The streak captures serial correlation in adverse oracle regimes; the spread filter removes adverse entry moments where oracle reliability is lower.
notes: PASS -- 12-date train window (20260308-20260320, 12 trading days): streak-spread-tight $4772.0/106428 trades vs simple $1984.0/132536 trades; delta_pnl=+140.52%, well above +5.0% gate. Win rate: 37.1% vs 35.6% (+1.5pp). Max drawdown: -1.41% vs -3.77% (improved). Skip rate: 19.7% (26,108 fewer trades). Improvement consistent across ALL 12 dates. Config: sigma=5, seed=42, horizon=30s. Slippage: both 0.0 (zero fill-cost model, see research/NOTES.md).

hypothesis: Order-book imbalance gating: condition the open leg of each oracle signal on top-of-book bid/ask size imbalance I = (q_bid - q_ask)/(q_bid + q_ask). For BUY orders, execute only when I >= +threshold; for SELL orders, only when I <= -threshold. Skip adversely-imbalanced opens; reduce-only orders always execute. The Lipton et al. (2013) empirical finding that book imbalance predicts the direction of the next mid-price tick motivates this: aligning entry direction with book imbalance reduces adverse selection in the open leg.
notes: PASS -- 12-date train window (20260308-20260320, excluding 20260314 no data): ob-imbalance-gate $4846.75/106990 trades vs simple $1984.0/132536 trades; delta_pnl=+144.29%, well above +5.0% gate. Win rate: 37.74% vs 35.57% (+2.17pp). Max drawdown: -2.21% vs -3.77% (improved). Skip rate: ~19.3% (25,546 fewer trades). Beat baseline on ALL 12 dates including turning losing days positive. Config: sigma=5, seed=42, horizon=30s, imbalance_threshold=0.0. Slippage: both 0.0 (zero fill-cost model, see research/NOTES.md). Sharpe improvement: +2.80 vs 0.91 for simple (+207.7%).

hypothesis: Volatility-regime trade-size scaling: estimate short-term realized mid-price volatility from recent quote ticks using two EWMs (fast halflife=20 ticks, slow halflife=120 ticks). Map the vol regime to a submission probability p = max(min_prob, exp(-sensitivity * max(0, vol_ratio - 1))) where vol_ratio = fast_vol / slow_vol. With 1-contract parent orders, continuous sizing is realized as probabilistic submission: p varies smoothly with vol, concentrating participation in calm regimes. Reduce-only orders always execute. Unlike binary gating algorithms (streak-spread-tight, ob-imbalance-gate), this uses a continuous, vol-magnitude-sensitive probability that decays smoothly with excess volatility.
notes: PASS -- 12-date train window (20260308-20260320, excluding 20260314 and 20260321 -- no data): vol-regime-sizer $2618.25/124002 trades vs simple $1984.00/132536 trades; delta_pnl=+31.97%, well above +5.0% gate. Win rate: 35.92% vs 35.57% (+0.35pp). Max drawdown: -0.030% vs -0.038% (improved). Trade reduction: ~6.4% (8,534 fewer trades). Improvement consistent across ALL 12 dates -- beats or matches baseline every date, including turning losing days into smaller losses. Config: sigma=5, seed=42, horizon=30s, fast_halflife=20, slow_halflife=120, sensitivity=2.0, min_prob=0.05. Slippage: both 0.0 (zero fill-cost model). Sharpe: 1.30 vs 0.91 (+42.9%). Note: algo PASS but Sharpe (1.30) is lower than prior passing algos (streak-spread-tight 2.76, ob-imbalance-gate 2.80) -- vol-regime sizer has less concentrated skipping, higher residual variance.

hypothesis: Microprice-vs-mid divergence gating: condition the open leg of each oracle signal on the signed divergence of the size-weighted microprice from the mid price. microprice = (bid_px * ask_sz + ask_px * bid_sz) / (bid_sz + ask_sz); delta = microprice - mid. When delta > +deadband (upward book pressure): favor BUY, skip SELL. When delta < -deadband (downward book pressure): favor SELL, skip BUY. When |delta| <= deadband: execute unconditionally. Reduce-only orders always execute. The microprice is a dollar-weighted pressure signal (Stoikov 2018) richer than raw quantity imbalance — it encodes both the direction and the fractional size asymmetry through the spread.
notes: PASS -- 12-date train window (20260308-20260320, excluding 20260314 and 20260321 -- no data): microprice-divergence-gate $4846.25/106990 trades vs simple $1984.00/132536 trades; delta_pnl=+144.27%, well above +5.0% gate. Win rate: 37.74% vs 35.57% (+2.17pp). Max drawdown: -0.022% vs -0.038% (improved). Skip rate: ~19.3% (25,546 fewer trades). Consistent improvement across ALL 12 dates. Config: sigma=5, seed=42, horizon=30s, microprice_deadband=0.0. Slippage: both 0.0 (zero fill-cost model). Sharpe: 2.80 vs 0.91 (+207.7%). Note: at deadband=0.0 the algorithm is functionally equivalent to ob-imbalance-gate (threshold=0.0) -- both skip when bid_size != ask_size and direction opposes pressure. Differentiation requires a nonzero deadband.

hypothesis: Passive-then-aggressive order laddering: for each open-leg oracle entry, first post a passive LIMIT order at same-side top-of-book (BUY at bid, SELL at ask) with a 5-tick timeout. If passive fills, capture the spread. If timeout fires, cancel and submit the original primary MarketOrder aggressively. Reduce-only orders always execute aggressively. Hypothesis: capturing spread on passive fills improves realized P&L vs always crossing, even after accounting for timeout-driven fallbacks at worse prices.
notes: FAIL -- 12-date train window (20260308-20260320, excluding 20260314 and 20260321 -- no data): passive-aggressive-ladder realized_pnl=-$1430.32 vs simple $1984.00; vs_baseline_pnl_pct=-172.09%, far below +5.0% gate. Sharpe=-1.053 vs 0.909 for simple. Trade count 132510 (similar to 132536 baseline). Root cause: adverse selection on passive fills -- passive BUY LIMIT at bid fills when market moves AGAINST the BUY signal (oracle adverse outcomes), while aggressive fallbacks after 5-tick timeout fire after price has already moved in the oracle direction (IS +$0.82/fallback vs +$0.14 baseline). Net: IS_total=$10,120 vs baseline $6,693 (+51.3 bps). Engine correctly models passive fills (fill_limit_inside_spread()=False). Mechanism is valid in theory but fails for directional oracle signals.

hypothesis: Adaptive participation sizing vs top-of-book depth: scale open-leg order submission probability as a continuous function of the current same-side top-of-book quantity at the moment the signal fires — p = clip(min_prob, 1.0, (q_same_side / depth_scale)^alpha). For BUY orders, q_same_side = ask_size (counterparty supply); for SELL orders, q_same_side = bid_size (counterparty demand). When the book is deep on the relevant side (q >= depth_scale), p=1.0 — full participation. When thin, p drops proportionally. Reduce-only orders always execute. Conditioning axis is absolute same-side depth magnitude, distinct from all prior algorithms (imbalance ratio, vol regime, microprice deviation, loss streak).
notes: FAIL -- 12-date train window (20260308-20260320, excluding 20260314 and 20260321 -- no data): depth-participation-sizer $1962.00/119549 trades vs simple $1984.00/132536 trades; delta_pnl=-1.11%, far below +5.0% gate. Sharpe: 1.10 vs 0.91 (+21%). IS_weighted_bps: 0.0332 vs 0.0375 (-11.4% improved IS). Trade reduction: 9.8% (12,987 fewer trades). Root cause: oracle signal quality is uncorrelated with same-side book depth in this dataset; skipping thin-book entries removed profitable and unprofitable trades equally, yielding a net P&L loss despite improved IS. Config: depth_scale=10, alpha=0.5, min_prob=0.10.

hypothesis: Time-of-day / session-phase temporal filter: condition the open leg of each oracle signal on the intraday wall-clock time. Skip entries during structurally low-quality session windows — open turbulence (08:30-09:00 CT), midday lull (11:45-12:15 CT), and pre-close ramp (15:00-15:15 CT). Execute normally during stable mid-session. Reduce-only orders always execute. The only information used is order.ts_init (UNIX ns, UTC), converted to CT with a fixed offset — no microstructure signal, no book data, no P&L history. Purely temporal and orthogonal to all prior algorithms.
notes: PASS -- 12-date train window (20260308-20260320, excluding 20260314 and 20260321 -- no data): session-clock-gate $2426.75/129136 trades vs simple $1984.00/132536 trades; delta_pnl=+22.32%, well above +5.0% gate. Win rate: 35.66% vs 35.57% (+0.09pp). Max drawdown: -0.036% vs -0.038% (improved). Skip rate: ~2.6% (3,400 fewer trades). Beat or matched baseline on ALL 12 dates -- never hurt. Config: sigma=5, seed=42, horizon=30s, utc_offset=-5 (CDT), skip windows: open 08:30-09:00 CT, midday 11:45-12:15 CT, pre-close 15:00-15:15 CT. Slippage: both 0.0 (zero fill-cost model). Sharpe: 1.15 vs 0.91 (+26.1%). Note: Sharpe (1.15) is lower than top passing algos (streak-spread-tight 2.76, ob-imbalance-gate 2.80) -- temporal filter has smaller skip rate (2.6% vs 19-20%) and thus less concentrated benefit.

hypothesis: Aggressor-flow gating: maintain a 10-second rolling window of signed net aggressor flow from trade prints (BUYER-aggressor volume minus SELLER-aggressor volume). Skip the open leg of a BUY signal when net flow <= -2.0 contracts (sell-dominated) and skip a SELL signal when net flow >= +2.0 contracts (buy-dominated). Reduce-only orders always execute. This conditions on realized marketable order flow -- trades that have already crossed the spread -- which is materially different from resting-book imbalance (ob-imbalance-gate, microprice-divergence-gate) which conditions on unaggressed limit orders. The hypothesis is that recent aggressor flow has stronger short-term directional predictive power because it reflects committed, revealed directional intent.
notes: PASS -- 12-date train window (20260308-20260320, excluding 20260314 and 20260321 -- no data): aggressor-flow-gate $3059.25/103947 trades vs simple $1984.00/132536 trades; delta_pnl=+54.20%, well above +5.0% gate. Win rate: 36.2% vs 35.6% (+0.6pp). Max drawdown: -0.0236% vs -0.0377% (improved). Skip rate: 21.6% (28,589 fewer trades). Beat baseline on 10/12 dates (20260308 slight underperform $135.50 vs $140.50; 20260311 near tie $395.50 vs $394.75). Config: sigma=5, seed=42, horizon=30s, window_seconds=10.0, flow_threshold=2.0. Slippage: both 0.0 (zero fill-cost model). Sharpe: 1.63 vs 0.91 (+79.3%). IS_weighted_bps: 0.0457 vs 0.0375 (+21.9% worse IS -- inherent tension in flow-based gating).
